  "per_column": [
    {"name": "is_low_score", "analytical_usefulness": 0.2, "source_groundedness": 0.5, "rationale": "This is a direct restatement of the original Score column and effectively the target label for the query 'what explains low scores?'. As an explanatory factor it is trivially redundant/circular. Grounded in Score, but note row 4 (medicinal cough medicine) marked is_low_score=1 with product_avg_score=2 seems consistent, though it is derived from Score not text."},
    {"name": "helpfulness_ratio", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "Cleanly derivable from HelpfulnessNumerator/Denominator. Gives a genuine axis to test whether unhelpful/contested reviews correlate with low scores. Values match source counts."},
    {"name": "review_length", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "rationale": "Raw character length is a generic feature but can be weakly useful (e.g., long complaints). Perfectly grounded from Text. Somewhat low leverage on its own for THIS query."},
    {"name": "word_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.3, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "rationale": "Largely redundant with review_length and generic token count; adds little independent analytical leverage. Fully grounded."},
    {"name": "has_exclamation", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "rationale": "Simple punctuation flag; may weakly signal emotional intensity but is generic. Grounded directly in Text."},
    {"name": "has_question", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "rationale": "Question-mark flag could hint at confusion/dissatisfaction but is generic and near-constant (94% zero). Grounded in Text."},
    {"name": "negative_word_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Count of negative lexicon terms gives a real axis relating tone to score. Grounded via text lexicon matching, though row 2 ('Not as Advertised', 'error') scored 0 negatives, suggesting lexicon misses—minor groundedness concern."},
    {"name": "positive_word_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Positive lexicon count is a useful sentiment axis for explaining scores. Reasonably grounded, values plausibly reflect text."},
    {"name": "sentiment_ratio", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Ratio derived from pos/neg counts; useful compact sentiment axis but partly redundant with the two count columns. Groundedness weakened because ratios appear high (0.5-0.75) even for negative rows (row 2 'Not as Advertised' = 0.5), reflecting the lexicon's poor coverage rather than true sentiment."},
    {"name": "summary_length", "analytical_usefulness": 0.3, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "rationale": "Generic length of Summary; low analytical leverage for explaining scores. Fully grounded in Summary."},
    {"name": "caps_ratio", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "Ratio of capital letters can proxy for shouting/emphasis, a plausible weak signal. Grounded from Text; values reasonable."},
    {"name": "product_avg_score", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Per-product average is a strong analytical axis (some products intrinsically rated low). Grounded in aggregating Score across ProductId, but the samples show product_avg_score equalling the row's own score (rows 2,4) which is suspicious—may reflect single-review products rather than true aggregation."},
    {"name": "user_avg_score", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Per-user average captures harsh vs lenient reviewers—genuine explanatory axis. Grounded via aggregation over UserId, but again samples show it equal to the row's own score, hinting at possible mis-aggregation."},
    {"name": "score_vs_product_avg", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.7, "rationale": "Deviation of a review from its product mean is a useful relative axis. Derived from Score and product_avg_score; some sample zeros stem from the questionable product_avg equalling own score."},
    {"name": "reviewer_is_harsh", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Flag for harsh reviewers is a useful grouping axis but largely derived from user_avg_score/this review's score and thus partly circular with is_low_score. Groundedness limited by the same aggregation ambiguity seen in user_avg_score."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
  "source_groundedness": 0.8,
  "rationale": "The set offers several genuinely useful axes for explaining low scores—helpfulness_ratio, negative/positive word counts, product_avg_score, user_avg_score, and score_vs_product_avg all give real grouping/modeling leverage. Weaknesses: is_low_score is a circular restatement of the target; word_count, summary_length, and several length/punctuation flags are generic and mutually redundant, adding limited leverage. Most values are well grounded in Text/Summary/helpfulness fields. The chief groundedness concern is the aggregate columns (product_avg_score, user_avg_score, and derivatives), where sample rows show the average equalling the row's own score—consistent with single-observation aggregation but leaving true cross-row aggregation unverified—plus a sentiment lexicon that misses clear negatives (row 2 'Not as Advertised' shows 0 negative words, sentiment 0.5). No confidently invented facts contradict the source, so groundedness remains reasonably high."
}
